titleEn: The Glory of Kings — The King of Persia and Tamar (ch. 77)
part: ch. 77 — The King of Persia and Tamar
about: The author explains why the king of Persia is of Shem's seed by retelling Genesis 38: Judah's two sons, the second refusing the levirate duty and struck dead by God, Tamar's disguise as a harlot and the pledges of staff, ring and cap, Judah's verdict that she is more righteous than he, and the birth of the twins Perez and Zerah. Persia is said to be named for Perez, whose line reigned there.

sentences.t: ፸፯ ፡ በእንተ ፡ ንጉሠ ፡ ፋርስ ።
sentences.l: 77. Concerning king-of Persia.
sentences.i: Chapter 77: Concerning the King of Persia
sentences.n: Chapter heading. በእንተ 'concerning' governs ንጉሠ ፋርስ 'king of Persia' in the construct state: the first noun of a chain loses its ending and is read 'of' the next (ንጉሠ ፋርስ, 'king-of Persia'). The country is ፋርስ (Fars); keep it apart from the name ፋሬስ (Perez) in the story below, which the chapter ties to it.

sentences.t: ወንጉሠ ፡ ፋርስኒ ፡ ዘርአ ፡ ሴም ፡ ውእቱ ፡ ወዘበእንቲአሁ ፡ ናየድዐክሙ ።
sentences.l: And-king-of Persia-also seed-of Shem he, and-that-which concerning-him we-will-inform-you.
sentences.i: Now the king of Persia is also of the seed of Shem, and we shall tell you about him.
sentences.n: ወ- 'and' opens the unit; -ኒ on ፋርስኒ is an enclitic 'also, indeed', carrying on from the Babylonian line of the previous chapter. ዘርአ ሴም is a construct chain, 'seed-of Shem': Shem is Noah's son, and the claim is that the Persian kings descend from him. ውእቱ is the pronoun 'he' used as the copula, 'he (is)'. ወዘበእንቲአሁ is ወ + ዘ ('that which') + በእንቲአሁ ('concerning him', a form of በእንተ + -ሁ). ናየድዐክሙ 'we shall inform you' is a 1st-plural imperfect of the causative stem (ʾa-stem) of ydʿ with the object suffix -ክሙ 'you (pl.)'; I take the root so, but the verb is not one I could confirm in Dillmann by sight (?).

sentences.t: ወለደ ፡ ይሁዳ ፡ ክልኤ ፡ ደቂቀ ፡ ወአእተወ ፡ ሎቱ ፡ ትዕማርሃ ፡ ለዘ ፡ ይልህቅ ፡ ወልዲ ፤
sentences.l: And-he-begot Judah two sons, and-he-brought-in for-him Tamar-her to-who he-is-older his-son;
sentences.i: Judah had two sons, and he gave Tamar in marriage to the elder of them;
sentences.n: The story is Genesis 38, the account of Judah and Tamar, told here with the names of Er and Onan left out: 'the older' is Er and 'the younger' (next unit) is Onan, implicit only. ወለደ 'he begot' is a plain 3ms perfect; ይሁዳ (Judah) is the subject after the verb. ክልኤ ደቂቀ is 'two' + the accusative plural of ወልድ 'son'. ወአእተወ is the causative of ተወ: 'he caused to enter', i.e. brought her in as a bride. ትዕማርሃ has a resumptive suffix -ሃ 'her' on the name, which I read as redundant (?). ለዘ ይልህቅ ወልዲ is 'to the one who is the elder, (his) son'; ዘ is the relative 'who', ይልህቅ 'he is grown/great'. The spelling ወልዲ is odd (expected ወልዱ 'his son'); I read it as 'his son' (?).

sentences.t: ወሞተ ፡ ወፈነዎ ፡ ለዘ ፡ ይንእስ ፡ ወልዲ ፡ ኀቤሃ ፡ ከመ ፡ ያቅም ፡ ለእኁሁ ፡ ዘርአ ፡ ኀበ ፡ ብእሲቱ ፡ እኁሁ ።
sentences.l: And-he-died, and-he-sent-him to-who he-is-younger son, to-her, that he-raise-up for-his-brother seed with wife-of his-brother.
sentences.i: The elder died, and Judah sent the younger son to her, to raise up offspring for his brother by his brother's wife.
sentences.n: The subject changes without a name: ሞተ 'he died' is the elder son; ፈነዎ 'he sent him' has Judah as its implied subject and -ዎ 'him' as object, re-stated by ለዘ ይንእስ ወልዲ 'the younger son' (ለ- marks the object here, 'to-who he-is-young'). ከመ ያቅም 'that he raise up' is ከመ + a subjunctive of the causative (ʾa-stem) of ቆመ 'stand': 'make stand, establish'. This is the levirate duty of Deuteronomy 25:5-10: a surviving brother must raise up seed for the dead one. ለእኁሁ 'for his brother' (እኁ + -ሁ); ኀበ ብእሲቱ እኁሁ 'with the wife of his brother', another construct chain.

sentences.t: ወውእቱኒ ፡ ገብረ ፡ ዘይጸልእ ፡ እግዚኣብሔር ፡ ወኢፈቀደ ፡ ከመ ፡ ያቅም ፡ ዘርአ ፡ ለእኁሁ ፡ በከመ ፡ አዘዞ ፡ አቡሁ ፡ ይሁዳ ፡ ወውእቱሰ ፡ ሶበ ፡ ይሰክብ ፡ ምስለ ፡ ትዕማር ፡ ያወፅእ ፡ ዘርኦ ፡ ውስተ ፡ ምድር ፡ ከመ ፡ ኢይትዐቈር ፡ ውስተ ፡ ከርሠ ፡ ዚአሃ ፡ ወኢይሰመይ ፡ ዘርአ ፡ እኁሁ ፤
sentences.l: And-he-also did what he-hates God, and-not-he-wished that he-raise-up seed for-his-brother as he-commanded-him his-father Judah; and-he-indeed, when he-lies with Tamar, he-brings-out his-seed to the-ground, that not-it-be-held in womb-of hers and-not it-be-called seed-of his-brother;
sentences.i: And he too did what God hates: he did not want to raise up offspring for his brother, as his father Judah had commanded him. Whenever he lay with Tamar he spilled his seed on the ground, so that it would not be held in her womb and not be called the seed of his brother;
sentences.n: This is Onan (Genesis 38:8-10), still unnamed. ወውእቱኒ is ወ + ውእቱ 'he' + ኒ 'also'; ውእቱሰ later has the contrastive -ሰ 'but, for his part'. ዘይጸልእ እግዚኣብሔር is a relative clause, 'that which God hates' (ዘ + imperfect ይጸልእ). ወኢፈቀደ is ኢ- 'not' + perfect ፈቀደ 'wished'. በከመ 'as' + አዘዞ 'he commanded him'. ሶበ ይሰክብ 'when he lies' is ሶበ + imperfect, here meaning 'whenever'; ያወፅእ is the causative of ወፅአ 'go out' (ʾa-stem): 'he brings out'. ዘርኦ is a spelling of ዘርኡ 'his seed'. Passive-type verbs: ኢይትዐቈር is the tä-stem (reflexive/passive) of ዐቈረ, 'be held, kept (in)' (?); ኢይሰመይ is the passive of ሰምየ 'name', 'be called'. ከርሠ ዚአሃ 'womb of hers': ዚአሃ is the possessive 'of her'.

sentences.t: አላ ፡ ይፈቅድ ፡ ከመ ፡ ያቅም ፡ ዘርአ ፡ እምብእሲቱ ፡ በስመ ፡ ዚአሁ ፤
sentences.l: But he-wishes that he-raise-up seed from-his-wife in-name-of his-own;
sentences.i: but he wanted to raise up offspring by his wife in his own name;
sentences.n: አላ 'but' sets his real wish against the duty. ይፈቅድ is the plain imperfect 'he wishes', used for his settled intent. እምብእሲቱ 'from his wife' is እም- 'from' + ብእሲት + -ሁ; the 'wife' is Tamar, who would be his own by the arrangement. በስመ ዚአሁ 'in name-of his-own': በ- 'in', ስመ in the construct state, ዚአሁ the independent possessive 'his own'. The point of the law was that a child be reckoned to the dead brother, not to the living one.

sentences.t: ወርእዮ ፡ እግዚኣብሔር ፡ እከየ ፡ ምግባሪሁ ፡ ሜጠ ፡ ገጾ ፡ እምኔሁ ፡ ወቀተሎ ።
sentences.l: And-having-seen-him God evil his-deeds, he-turned his-face from-him and-he-killed-him.
sentences.i: And God saw his evil deeds, turned his face from him, and killed him.
sentences.n: ወርእዮ is the gerund of ርእየ 'see' with ወ-: 'and seeing (he)', the subject being God, i.e. 'God having seen'. -ዮ here is the ending of the gerund, not an object suffix; the verb that follows is the main one. እከየ is the accusative of እኩይ 'evil'. ምግባሪሁ 'his deeds' (the plural of ምግባር). ሜጠ ገጾ 'he turned his face' is the idiom of withdrawing favour; ወቀተሎ 'and he killed him' (ቀተለ + -ሎ). Compare Genesis 38:10: what Onan did displeased the Lord, and he put him to death.

sentences.t: ወአግብኣ ፡ ይሁዳ ፡ ሐሙሃ ፡ ለትዕማር ፡ ወአእተዋ ፡ ውስተ ፡ ቤተ ፡ አቡሃ ፡ ወይቤሎሙ ፡ ለአዝማዲሃ ፡ ዕቀብዋ ፡ ለዛቲ ፡ እስራኤላዊት ፡ ወኢታርኵስዋ ፡ ኀበ ፡ ባዕድ ፡ እስመ ፡ ብየ ፡ ንኡሰ ፡ ሕፃነ ፡ ለእመ ፡ አልሀቆ ፡ እግዚኣብሔር ፡ እሁቦ ፡ ኪያሃ ።
sentences.l: And-he-sent-her-back Judah her-father-in-law to-Tamar and-he-brought-her-in to house-of her-father, and-he-said-to-them to-her-kinsfolk: Keep this Israelite-woman and-do-not-defile-her to other, because there-is-to-me young small-boy; if he-makes-grow-him God, I-give-him her.
sentences.i: Judah, her father-in-law, sent Tamar back, and brought her into her father's house, and said to her kinsfolk: Keep this Israelite woman, and do not let her be defiled with another man, for I have a young child; if God makes him grow up, I shall give her to him.
sentences.n: ወአግብኣ is the causative (ʾa-stem) of ገብአ 'return' with -ኣ 'her': 'he made her return'. ሐሙሃ 'her father-in-law' (ሐም + -ሃ) stands in apposition to ይሁዳ, and ለትዕማር repeats the object. ወአእተዋ is 'and he brought her in' (causative of ተወ). Imperatives: ዕቀብዋ 'keep her' (2mp, with -ዋ 'her'), ወኢታርኵስዋ 'and do not defile her' (ኢ- + 2mp jussive of the causative of ርኩስ 'unclean'); ኀበ ባዕድ is 'to/with another (man)'. ብየ is 'there is to me' (ብ- 'there is' + የ 'me'), the Geʿez way to say 'I have'. This younger child is Shelah of Genesis 38:11, whom the text leaves unnamed. ለእመ 'if'; አልሀቆ 'he makes him grow' (causative of ልሀቀ) and እሁቦ ኪያሃ 'I give him her' (ኪያሃ is the independent object pronoun 'her').

sentences.t: ወእንዘ ፡ ትነብር ፡ ምዕስብት ፡ ውስተ ፡ ቤተ ፡ አቡሃ ፡ ናሁ ፡ መጽአ ፡ ይሁዳ ፡ ሐሙሃ ፡ ውስተ ፡ መራዕየ ፡ አዕጻ ፡ ዳተ ፡ አባግዒሁ ፡ ከመ ፡ ይቅርጽ ፡ ፀምረ ፡ ምስለ ፡ ብዙኅ ፡ ፍግዓ ፡ ወተድላ ፤
sentences.l: And-while she-dwells widow in house-of her-father, behold he-came Judah her-father-in-law to pastures-of folds-of his-sheep to shear wool with much joy and-delight;
sentences.i: While she was living as a widow in her father's house, Judah, her father-in-law, came to the pastures where his sheep were folded, to shear the wool with great joy and merrymaking;
sentences.n: ወእንዘ 'and while' takes the imperfect (ትነብር 'she dwells'). ምዕስብት 'widow' (?); ምዕስብና in the next unit is 'widowhood', which supports it. ናሁ 'behold' marks a turn in the story. The word-break in አዕጻ ፡ ዳተ is a split of አዕጻዳት, 'enclosures, folds', the plural of ዐጸድ; so መራዕየ አዕጻዳተ አባግዒሁ is a chain 'pastures-of folds-of his-sheep' (?). ከመ ይቅርጽ 'to shear' (ከመ + subjunctive; ቀርጸ taken as 'cut, shear' (?)); ፀምር is 'wool'. ብዙኅ ፍግዓ ወተድላ 'much joy and delight', with accusatives.

sentences.t: ወትዕማርሰ ፡ ሶበ ፡ ሰምዐት ፡ ከመ ፡ መጽአ ፡ ሐሙሃ ፡ ገደፈት ፡ እምላዕሌሃ ፡ አልባሰ ፡ ምዕስብና ፡ ወተረሰየት ፡ በአልባሰ ፡ ክብር ፡ ወተገልበበት ፡ በአምሳለ ፡ ዘማት ፡ ወሖረት ፡ እንተ ፡ ድኅሬሁ ፡ ወነበረት ።
sentences.l: And-Tamar-indeed when she-heard that he-came her-father-in-law, she-cast-off from-upon-her garments-of widowhood, and-she-made-herself in-garments-of honour, and-she-veiled-herself in-likeness-of harlot, and-she-went that behind-him and-she-sat.
sentences.i: But when Tamar heard that her father-in-law had come, she took off her widow's clothes, dressed herself in fine garments, wrapped herself in a veil like a harlot's, went out behind him, and sat down.
sentences.n: ወትዕማርሰ: ወ- + name + -ሰ, the contrastive 'but Tamar for her part'. ሰምዐት, ገደፈት, ሖረት, ነበረት are all 3fs perfects (ending -ት). ገደፈት እምላዕሌሃ is 'she threw off from upon her'; አልባሰ ምዕስብና is a construct chain, 'garments-of widowhood', as is አልባሰ ክብር 'garments-of honour' (fine, splendid clothes). ተረሰየት is the tä-stem of ረሰየ 'set, make': 'she made herself up, was arrayed'. ተገልበበት is a tä-stem of the four-letter ገልበበ 'wrap, veil' (?). Compare Genesis 38:14-15, where she veils her face and sits where Judah will pass. በአምሳለ ዘማት 'in the likeness of a harlot'. The last clause, ወሖረት እንተ ድኅሬሁ, I read as 'she went (the way) behind him', taking እንተ as a preposition 'toward' (?).

sentences.t: ወለአከ ፡ ኀቤሃ ፡ እንዘ ፡ ይብል ፡ እፈቅድ ፡ እባእ ፡ ኀቤኪ ፤
sentences.l: And-he-sent to-her saying: I-wish I-may-enter to-you;
sentences.i: And he sent word to her: I want to come in to you;
sentences.n: ለአከ 'he sent' (a message or a messenger), with እንዘ ይብል 'saying' (እንዘ + imperfect ይብል, the standard way to introduce speech). እፈቅድ 'I wish' and እባእ 'I may enter' are 1cs forms (the second a subjunctive of ቦአ, with no ከመ). ኀቤኪ 'to you' (feminine -ኪ). In Genesis 38:16 Judah goes to her himself; this version has him send.

sentences.t: ወትቤሎ ፡ ምንተ ፡ ትሁበኒ ፡ ዐስብየ ፤
sentences.l: And-she-said-to-him: What will-you-give-me, my-wage?
sentences.i: And she said to him: What will you give me as my wage?
sentences.n: ወትቤሎ 'and she said to him' (ትቤ 3fs imperfect of በለ 'say', with -ሎ 'to him'); the verb ይቤ / ትቤ is the narrative 'said' throughout. ትሁበኒ 'you will give me' is 2ms imperfect of ወሀበ + -ኒ 'me'. ዐስብየ 'my wage' (ዐስብ + የ 'my'). Genesis 38:16: 'What will you give me?'

sentences.t: ወይቤላ ፡ እፌኑ ፡ ለኪ ፡ ነግሀ ፡ በጽባሕ ፡ ማሕስአ ፡ ጠሊ ፤
sentences.l: And-he-said-to-her: I-will-send to-you at-dawn in-the-morning kid (?) of-goats;
sentences.i: And he said to her: I shall send you a kid in the morning, at daybreak;
sentences.n: ወይቤላ 'and he said to her'. እፌኑ 'I will send' (1cs of ፈነወ). ነግሀ በጽባሕ 'at dawn, in the morning' is two time words in a row. ማሕስአ ጠሊ: ጠሊ is a young goat or kid; ማሕስአ I cannot parse with confidence, and I take it as a word of the same field, 'kid, young one' (?), so the English just says 'a kid'. This is the kid of Genesis 38:17.

sentences.t: ወትቤሎ ፡ ሀበኒ ፡ አኅዘ ፡ እስከ ፡ ትሁበኒ ፡ ጠሊተ ፤
sentences.l: And-she-said-to-him: Give-me a-pledge until you-give-me the-kid;
sentences.i: And she said to him: Give me a pledge until you give me the kid;
sentences.n: ሀበኒ 'give me' is the imperative of ወሀበ + -ኒ. አኅዘ is the accusative of አኅዝ 'pledge, security' (?); from the context, which matches Genesis 38:17-18. እስከ 'until' takes the imperfect (ትሁበኒ). ጠሊተ is the feminine accusative of ጠሊ, 'a she-kid'.

sentences.t: ወወሀባ ፡ በትረ ፡ ወሕልቀተ ፡ ወቆብዐ ፡ እንተ ፡ መትሕተ ፡ አክሊሉ ።
sentences.l: And-he-gave-her staff and-ring and-cap which beneath his-crown.
sentences.i: And he gave her his staff, his ring, and the cap that he wore beneath his crown.
sentences.n: ወወሀባ 'and he gave her' (ወሀበ + -ኣ). The pledge, as in Genesis 38:18, is the identifying property of a man: በትረ 'staff' (accusative), ሕልቀተ 'ring' (a seal-ring) and ቆብዐ 'cap'. እንተ is the feminine relative 'which', agreeing with ቆብዕ; መትሕተ is the construct of መትሕት 'beneath', so 'beneath-of his-crown', with አክሊሉ 'his crown'.

sentences.t: ወቦአ ፡ ኀቤሃ ፡ ወነሥአት ፡ ወሖረት ፡ ውስተ ፡ ቤታ ፡ ወፈነወ ፡ ላቲ ፡ በጽባሕ ፡ ጠሌ ፤
sentences.l: And-he-entered to-her and-she-took and-she-went to her-house, and-he-sent to-her in-the-morning kid;
sentences.i: He went in to her; she took the pledges and went to her house; and in the morning he sent her the kid;
sentences.n: Two subjects alternate without a name: ቦአ 'he entered' is Judah; ነሥአት and ሖረት (ending -ት) are Tamar; ፈነወ 'he sent' is Judah again. The sentence has no object for 'took', so I supply 'the pledges' (?). ቤታ is ቤት + -ሃ, 'her house'; ላቲ is 'to her'. ጠሌ is a spelling of ጠሊ, 'kid'.

sentences.t: ወተስእሉ ፡ አግብርቲሁ ፡ ወይቤሉ ፡ አይቴ ፡ ውእቱ ፡ ቤተ ፡ ዘማት ፡ ወይቤልዎሙ ፡ አልቦ ፡ ውስተ ፡ ሀገርነ ፡ ዘማት ፤
sentences.l: And-they-asked his-servants and-they-said: Where is that house-of harlot? and-they-said-to-them: There-is-not in our-city harlot;
sentences.i: His servants asked, and said: Where is that harlot's house? And the townsmen answered: There is no harlot in our city;
sentences.n: ተስእሉ is the perfect of ተስእለ 'inquire', 3mp. The servants are Judah's, sent with the kid (previous unit). ወይቤልዎሙ 'and they said to them' (ይቤሉ + -ሙ), the answer coming from the local people. አይቴ 'where?'; ቤተ ዘማት is a construct chain 'house-of harlot' (the odd ውእቱ before it is the demonstrative 'that') (?). አልቦ 'there is not' (ኢ- + ብ-), the opposite of the ብየ 'I have' above. ሀገርነ 'our city' (ሀገር + -ነ). Genesis 38:21-22 has the same question and the same denial.

sentences.t: ወገብኡ ፡ ውስተ ፡ ሀገሮሙ ፡ ወነገርዎ ፡ ከመ ፡ አልቦ ፡ ውስተ ፡ ሀገሮሙ ፡ ዘማት ፤
sentences.l: And-they-returned to their-city and-they-told-him that there-is-not in their-city harlot;
sentences.i: They went back to their own city and told him that there was no harlot in that place;
sentences.n: ገብኡ 'they returned' (3mp of ገብአ); ወነገርዎ 'and they told him' (ነገረ + -ዎ). Both ሀገሮሙ ('their city') have -ሙ; the second I take as the city where they had asked, the first as the servants' own city (?).

sentences.t: ወይቤ ፡ ይሁዳ ፡ ኅድጉአ ፡ ፈቃደ ፡ እግዚኣብሔር ፡ ለይኩን ።
sentences.l: And-he-said Judah: Leave-it; will-of God let-it-be.
sentences.i: And Judah said: Let it be; may God's will be done.
sentences.n: ኅድጉአ is the 2mp imperative of ኀደገ 'leave, abandon', with a suffix 'it/her' (the spelling -አ for -ኣ). ፈቃደ እግዚኣብሔር 'will-of God', a construct chain and the subject of ለይኩን, which is the jussive 'let it be' (ለ- + ይኩን). The tone is that of letting the matter drop, rather than the pledge-recovery worry of Genesis 38:23.

sentences.t: ወእምዝ ፡ ፀንሰት ፡ ትዕማር ፡ ወነገርዎ ፡ ለሐሙሃ ፡ ከመ ፡ ፀንሰት ፤
sentences.l: And-after-this she-conceived Tamar, and-they-told-him to-her-father-in-law that she-conceived;
sentences.i: After this Tamar became pregnant, and they told her father-in-law that she was with child;
sentences.n: ወእምዝ 'and after this' (እም- 'from' + ዝ 'this'). ፀንሰት 'she conceived' (3fs perfect of ፀንሰ), repeated after ከመ. ወነገርዎ 'they told him', an impersonal plural, with ለሐሙሃ repeating the person told. Genesis 38:24: 'about three months later it was told Judah.'

sentences.t: ወሖረ ፡ ወነሥአ ፡ መላህቅተ ፡ እስራኤል ፡ ኀበ ፡ አቡሃ ፡ ለትዕማር ፡ ወይቤሎ ፡ አቅርብ ፡ ሊተ ፡ ወለትከ ፡ ፅንስተ ፡ ከመ ፡ ንውግራ ፡ በአእባ ፡ ን ፡ በከመ ፡ አዘዘ ፡ ሙሴ ፡ እስመ ፡ አኅሰረት ፡ ቤተ ፡ እስራኤል ።
sentences.l: And-he-went and-he-took elders-of Israel to father-of Tamar, and-he-said-to-him: Bring-forward to-me and-your-daughter pregnant, that we-stone-her with-stones as he-commanded Moses, because she-has-diminished house-of Israel.
sentences.i: He went and took the elders of Israel to Tamar's father and said to him: Bring me your daughter, who is pregnant, so that we may stone her, as Moses commanded, because she has brought loss on the house of Israel.
sentences.n: The subject of ሖረ and ነሥአ is Judah. መላህቅተ እስራኤል 'elders-of Israel' is a construct chain (መላህቅት is the plural of ልሁቅ 'elder'). Tamar's father is given as አቡሃ ለትዕማር 'her father, of Tamar'. አቅርብ is the imperative of the causative of ቀርበ, 'bring near'; ሊተ 'to me'; ወለትከ 'your daughter' (ወለት + -ከ); ፅንስተ is the feminine accusative of ፅንስ, 'pregnant'. ንውግራ 'that we stone her' is 1cp jussive of ወግረ 'stone' + -ራ. The odd split in በአእባ ፡ ን is one word, በአእባን 'with stones' (አእባን, plural of እብን); it is written whole at the end of unit 22. Stoning for unchastity: Deuteronomy 22:20-24 (the text names Moses as the lawgiver); in Genesis 38:24 the penalty is burning. አኅሰረት is the causative of ኀሰረ 'lack' so 'she has made lack, brought loss to' (?); ቤተ እስራኤል 'house-of Israel'.

sentences.t: ወነገርዋ ፡ ለትዕማር ፡ አቡሃ ፡ ወአዝማዲሃ ፡ ከመ ፡ ከመዝ ፡ ይቤ ፡ ሐሙሃ ፤
sentences.l: And-they-told-her to-Tamar her-father and-her-kinsfolk that thus he-said her-father-in-law;
sentences.i: Her father and her kinsfolk told Tamar that Judah, her father-in-law, had spoken in this way;
sentences.n: ወነገርዋ 'and they told her' has the subject after the verb (አቡሃ ወአዝማዲሃ, 'her father and her kinsfolk'), and ለትዕማር repeats the object. ከመ ከመዝ 'that thus' introduces the report; ከመዝ is 'thus, in this way'. ይቤ ሐሙሃ 'he said, her father-in-law', so Judah goes unnamed here.

sentences.t: ወአውፅአት ፡ ሕልቀተ ፡ ወበትረ ፡ ወቆብዐ ፡ ወወሀበት ፡ ለአቡሃ ፡ ወለአዝማዲሃ ፡ ወትቤሎሙ ፡ ባዕለ ፡ ዝንቱአ ፡ ዘአስሐተኒ ፡ ወይውግሩኒ ፡ ምስሌሁ ፡ በአእባን ።
sentences.l: And-she-brought-out ring and-staff and-cap, and-she-gave to-her-father and-to-her-kinsfolk, and-she-said-to-them: Owner-of this-one who made-me-err, and-let-them-stone-me with-him with-stones.
sentences.i: She brought out the ring, the staff, and the cap, gave them to her father and her kinsfolk, and said to them: The owner of these is the one who led me astray; and they may stone me with him, with stones.
sentences.n: አውፅአት is the causative of ወፅአ ('go out'), so 'she brought out'. She gives back the three items of Judah's pledge. ባዕለ ዝንቱአ: ባዕል 'owner, master' (here the construct before ዝንቱ 'this') and the odd final አ on ዝንቱአ, which I take as an enclitic on ዝንቱ, 'this one' (?). ዘአስሐተኒ is 'he who made me err': a relative ዘ + the causative of ሰሕተ 'err' + -ኒ 'me', i.e. 'seduced' (?). ወይውግሩኒ is 'and they stone me': 3mp imperfect of ወግረ + -ኒ, here read as a challenge or consequence, 'let them' (?). This is Genesis 38:25, where she sends the objects with the words 'by the man to whom these belong I am with child.'

sentences.t: ወሶበ ፡ ርእየ ፡ ይሁዳ ፡ ንዋዮ ፡ አእመረ ፡ ወይቤ ፡ ጸድቀት ፡ ትዕማር ፡ እምኔየ ፤
sentences.l: And-when he-saw Judah his-goods he-recognised, and-he-said: Righteous-is Tamar from-me;
sentences.i: When Judah saw his belongings he recognised them, and said: Tamar is more righteous than I;
sentences.n: ንዋዮ is a spelling of ንዋዩ 'his goods, belongings'. አእመረ 'he recognised, knew' (causative-stem verb). ጸድቀት is a 3fs perfect, 'she is/has been righteous', and እምኔየ is 'from me', i.e. 'than I' (the comparative use of እም-). This is Genesis 38:26: 'She is more righteous than I'.

sentences.t: ወኀደጋ ፡ ወአተወ ፡ ቤቶ ።
sentences.l: And-he-left-her and-he-entered his-house.
sentences.i: He let her be, and went into his house.
sentences.n: ወኀደጋ 'and he left her' (ኀደገ + -ጋ; the same verb as ኅድጉአ above, the leaving of an issue). አተወ 'he entered' is the simple stem, in contrast to the causative አእተወ above (unit 2). ቤቶ is a spelling of ቤቱ 'his house'. The text does not say whether she was taken to wife again; Genesis 38:26 says he knew her no more.

sentences.t: ወወለደት ፡ ትዕማር ፡ መንታ ፡ ክልኤተ ፡ ሕዝበ ፡ ፋሬስ ፡ ወዛራ ፤
sentences.l: And-she-bore Tamar twins, two peoples (?): Perez and-Zerah;
sentences.i: Tamar bore twins, two peoples (?): Perez and Zerah;
sentences.n: ወለደት 'she bore' (ወለደ + -ት, 3fs). መንታ is 'twins' and ክልኤተ the feminine accusative of 'two'. ሕዝበ 'people, nation' may stand loosely for the two heads of lines; I give it plainly and mark it (?). ፋሬስ and ዛራ are Perez and Zerah (Genesis 38:27-30, where Perez breaks out first and Zerah's hand carries the scarlet thread). The Geʿez ፋሬስ (Perez) is not to be confused with ፋርስ (Persia).

sentences.t: ወተሐንጸት ፡ ፋርስ ፡ በስመ ፡ ፋሬስ ፡ ወነግሠ ፡ ላዕሌሃ ፡ ውእቱ ፡ ወዘርኡ ፡ እምድኅሬሁ ፡ ወተሰምዩ ፡ ፈረሳዊያን ።
sentences.l: And-was-built Persia in-name-of Perez, and-he-reigned over-her he and-his-seed after-him, and-they-were-called Persians.
sentences.i: Persia was founded under the name of Perez, and he reigned over it, he and his seed after him; and they were called Persians.
sentences.n: ተሐንጸት is the passive (tä-stem) of ሐነጸ 'build', with a feminine ending since ፋርስ (the land) is feminine here; ላዕሌሃ 'over her'. በስመ ፋሬስ 'in name-of Perez' (construct chain): the book derives the land's name from Perez, a play on ፋሬስ and ፋርስ. ነግሠ 'he reigned'; ውእቱ 'he' stands as emphatic subject, with ወዘርኡ 'and his seed' added after. እምድኅሬሁ 'after him'. ተሰምዩ is the tä-stem plural, 'were called', and ፈረሳዊያን (plural of ፈረሳዊ) I read as 'Persians' (?). That this derivation is the book's own, not a historical one, is plain.

sentences.t: ናሁኬ ፡ ተዐውቀ ፡ ንጉሠ ፡ ፋርስ ፡ ከመ ፡ ዘርአ ፡ ሴም ፡ ውእቱ ፨ ፨ ፨ ፨
sentences.l: Behold-then it-is-known king-of Persia that seed-of Shem he. ፨ ፨ ፨ ፨
sentences.i: So now it is known that the king of Persia is of the seed of Shem.
sentences.n: ናሁኬ is ናሁ 'behold' + -ኬ 'then, so', closing the argument opened in the first unit. ተዐውቀ 'it is known' is the passive (tä-stem) of ዐወቀ, and its subject is the king himself,  ንጉሠ ፋርስ ('king-of Persia'), then ከመ ዘርአ ሴም ውእቱ 'that he is the seed of Shem'. The chain of descent is Shem to Judah to Perez, from whom the Persian kings are said to come. The four ፨ marks close the chapter.
